events.name: Bash

input.command:
\
BASE_REF="origin/main" && \
HEAD_REF="HEAD" && \
BASE_ROOT=".rgctl-base" && \
LIMITS_SPEC="max-mem-mb=4096,threads=1"

# Check if base artifact already exists
if [ -f "${BASE_ROOT}/.rgctl/graph.snapshot.bin" ]; then
  echo "✓ Using existing base artifact at ${BASE_ROOT}"
else
  echo "Creating base artifact for ${BASE_REF}..."
  git fetch origin main 2>/dev/null || true
  WT=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rgctl-base-wt.XXXXXX")
  cleanup_wt() { git worktree remove --force "$WT" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -rf "$WT"; }
  trap cleanup_wt EXIT
  git worktree add --detach "$WT" "$BASE_REF"
  (
    cd "$WT"
    rgctl discover . --with-limits "${LIMITS_SPEC}"
  )
  mkdir -p .rgctl-base
  rm -rf .rgctl-base/.rgctl
  cp -a "$WT/.rgctl" .rgctl-base/
  cleanup_wt
  trap - EXIT
  echo "✓ Base artifact created"
fi

# Verify base artifact
test -f "${BASE_ROOT}/.rgctl/graph.snapshot.bin" && echo "✓ Base graph ready"

✓ Using existing base artifact at .rgctl-base
✓ Base graph ready

events.text: If I only want to block new violations, how should we scope the gate?

To block **only new violations**, scope your CI gate to exit non-zero only when `violations_summary.new > 0`:

```bash
rgctl -f json review check --policy-file policy.json \
  --bisect --base-artifact .rgctl-base --base-ref origin/main --head-ref HEAD \
  | jq -e '.violations_summary.new == 0' || exit 1
```

This passes the gate if no *new* violations are introduced, regardless of `existing` or `regression` counts. Pre-existing violations on main won't block the merge.

Alternatively, if you want to also allow regressions to slip through (not recommended):

```bash
jq -e '(.violations_summary.new + .violations_summary.regression) == 0'
```

The cleaner approach: check only `.new > 0` to enforce forward progress without penalizing legacy debt on main.
